% 09.01.2026 I.A. 506/2026 (Exemption from pre-institution Mediation)
1. This is an Application filed by the Plaintiff seeking exemption from instituting pre-litigation Mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Court Act, 2015.

2. As the present matter contemplates urgent interim relief, in light of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Yamini Manohar v. T.K.D. Keerthi, (2024) 5 SCC 815, exemption from the requirement of pre-institution Mediation is granted.

9. For the reasons stated therein, exemption is allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
10. The original and/or clear and typed copies of the documents with proper margins of the dim annexures be filed within six weeks with an advance copy to the defendants.
11. Accordingly, the application stands disposed of.
I.A. 507/2026 (Interim injunction)

12. The plaintiff claims to manufacture goods not limited to Ayurvedic Oil, Ayurvedic Capsule,
Medicinal and pharmaceutical preparations under its trademark and copyrights not limited to "HAMMER OF THOR/ This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/01/2026 at 20:36:58 /HAMMER OF THOREX/ HAMMER OF GOLD/ "from as early as year 2013 and being sold through e-commerce platforms as well as their own websites.

13. Plaintiff claims that defendant nos. 1 to 3 have attempted to secure registrations from the impugned mark "D' HAMMER THOR/ / /HERBAL OF HAMMER" and have taken the malicious actions of filing rectification against the plaintiff's registered marks.

The plaintiff further claims that defendant nos. 1 to 5 are sellers of the impugned goods on the platform of defendant nos. 6 to 12 who are alleged to be advertising, marketing and selling counterfeit goods under the impugned marks.
14.

On account of the aforesaid infringement of the trademark, copyrights and trade dress of the plaintiff's products, the present suit has been preferred seeking permanent and mandatory injunction against copyright infringement, trademark passing off and unfair competition against the defendants.

sentences.text: Ms. Roda, learned counsel for the plaintiff submits that as far back as on 10.04.2013, the plaintiff had launched its products under the mark "HAMMER OF THOR" in support whereof she relies upon the tax/sales invoices filed alongwith the present suit.

She submits that subsequently, the copyright of the artistic work "HAMMER GOLD/ " was obtained on 01.01.2021 and for the artistic work "HAMMER OF THOR/ ", copyright registration was obtained on 01.10.2019.
She also submits that even the trademark was This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/01/2026 at 20:36:58 registered by the trademarks registry on 23.09.2017, which is depicted as under:-
16.

Learned counsel submits that the plaintiff has invested huge amounts in advertisement and have a steady growth of sales and has a substantial increase in the turnover, which is indicated in the certificate issued by the Chartered Accountant from the financial year 2013-14 to the year 2021-22, and even subsequent thereto.

She states that apart from the above, the plaintiff has been vigilant enough to protect his trademark and artistic work against other third parties in this Court wherein interim order in favour of the plaintiff have been passed which are also clear from the orders of this Court in CS(COMM) 863/2022 and CS(COMM) 863/2023 dated 12.12.2022 and 07.12.2023 respectively.

17. Predicated on the above, Ms. Roda states that the defendants with a dishonest intention and to ride on the goodwill of the plaintiff, gathered over substantial number of years, are unauthorizedly using the impugned trademarks which are deceptively similar to that of the registered trademark and artwork of the plaintiff.

She submits that the infringement and passing off are apparent from the fact that though the defendants sought registration of their marks in the year 2021, yet had abandoned the same after an opposition was filed by the plaintiff.
The order of abandonment dated 24.11.2023 is relied on by the plaintiff.

She also invites attention to the counter statement of the defendant to the rectification application filed by the plaintiff to submit that the defendant itself admit that they have adopted the trademark "D HAMMER THOR/ This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/01/2026 at 20:36:58 "
on 20.02.2024 and claimed to have been continuously using the same since then.

According to her,
this is an admission of having adopted the said mark much after the prior user and registration of the trademark of the plaintiff.
She states that in such circumstances, it is clear that the defendants cannot be permitted to use the impugned trademark or the art work under any circumstances.

Additionally, she submits that the defendants are violating the statutory Rules and Regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 since the products listed in Class-V are medicinal in nature.

sentences.text: After having heard learned counsel for the plaintiff and perusing the impugned marks, prima facie it appears that the defendants are infringing on the registered trademark and art work of the plaintiff by unauthorizedly using the impugned marks and art work.
19. Having regard to the fact that plaintiff is the owner and prior user of the trademark and art work since 2013, the balance of convenience also appears to be in favour of the applicant/plaintiff.
Equally, it appears, prima facie, that the plaintiff has made out a case of passing off also.
It has to be borne in mind that not only are the packaging, trademark and the art work deceptively similar, but also the products manufactured and sold are similar.
It is also relevant to note that even the consumer base, to whom such goods are offered are also common.
Apparently the applicant/plaintiff is likely to suffer irreparable loss and injury which may not be completely compensated in monetary terms.
20. In that view of the matter, this Court is of the prima facie opinion that a case for ad- interim injunction is made out.

Mr. Naman Tandon has entered appearance on behalf of defendant no.6 and being an intermediary on whose e-commerce website the impugned products are being sold and submits that the defendant no.6 would comply with any orders that may be passed by this Court.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

Accordingly, the following directions are passed:-
i.

The Defendant nos.1 to 5, its partners, agents, employees, and all other persons acting for or on their behalf, are restrained from manufacturing, distributing,
exporting, selling, offering for sale, advertising, promoting, displaying, or in any manner using the marks or trade names, trademarks namely "D' HAMMER THOR/ /
/HERBAL OF HAMMER", and/or from using any other mark which is deceptively similar or identical to the plaintiff's trademark.

ii. Defendant nos.1 to 5 are directed to remove advertisement and listing from third party websites and immediately make a full and fair disclosure of any other online advertisement of its goods on any other website.

iii. Defendant nos.6 to 12 are directed to take down all the infringing listings of defendant nos.1 to 5 on their platform and make a full and fair disclosure to the plaintiff of the full details involved in the manufacturing, marketing, distributing and selling the impugned products along with the details of sales made by them.
22. Let the plaintiff comply with the requirement of Order XXXIX Rule 3 of the CPC within one week from today.
